focus_areas: Geometric separation of cursorial legs from sandy background
Texture consistency and halo detection at body-sand interface
Leg count and joint connectivity verification
Spatial grounding of the beetle on the uneven sand surface
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the junction where the legs meet the sand; use the geometric depth auditor to ensure they are not merging with the ground. Verify that the mandibles are symmetrical and physically attached to the head capsule. Check for any 'halo' effects or unnatural blurring around the metallic elytra against the rough sand texture. Ensure all six legs are topologically connected to the thorax despite the camouflage.
image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of a tiger beetle (Cicindelinae) positioned on coarse sandy ground. The beetle exhibits characteristic metallic green and bronze coloration with distinct pale cream-colored markings on its elytra. It has long, slender legs adapted for running, prominent compound eyes, and visible mandibles. The antennae are long and thread-like. The background consists of out-of-focus sand grains.
